brow: Aggregated snapshot · open-source compilation · not official reporting
editionNote: Morning edition. It covers the 24 hours to 05:10 CET on 30 October; new research covers 17:10 CET on 29 October to 05:10 CET on 30 October, items from the previous edition still inside the 24 hours were carried, and stories with new developments are marked as follow-ups.

theaters.heading: Battlefield, long-range strikes, and peace diplomacy in Russia's war on Ukraine

items.title: More Than 350,000 Lose Power Around Ukraine's Dnipro After Evening Strikes
items.lede: Pumping stations switched to generators as crews worked through the night, hours after a drone set a college dormitory ablaze in the same city.

sections.text: Russian forces struck Dnipro, Ukraine, again late on Thursday 29 October, leaving more than 350,000 subscribers in the city and nearby settlements without electricity, regional head Oleksandr Hanzha said [1][2][3]. Hanzha said repair crews were at work and water and sewage pumping stations were being switched to generators [2][1]. Energy firm DTEK said high-voltage grid equipment was damaged [1][2]. Earlier that evening a drone hit the top floor of a vocational college dormitory in Dnipro, injuring two girls aged 15 and 16, Hanzha and Mayor Borys Filatov said [4]. No Russian comment was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the outage, because Interfax-Ukraine, Ukrainska Pravda, and the Kyiv Independent carry the same on-record figure from the regional head. The figure is preliminary. The dormitory strike rests on one outlet.

items.title: Moscow Shuts All Four Airports as Drones Return for a Second Night
items.lede: Flights were diverted to other cities after Russia's capital came under attack from 23:00 local time, a night after more than 460 flights were disrupted.

sections.text: Russia's aviation agency Rosaviatsia imposed restrictions at Moscow's Domodedovo, Vnukovo, Zhukovsky, and Sheremetyevo airports on Thursday night, 29 October, as drones approached the capital, and Yaroslavl airport also closed [5][6]. Komsomolskaya Pravda said the restrictions began at 22:50 Moscow time (20:50 CET) and that more than 20 Moscow-bound flights were diverted to other cities, including 12 bound for Vnukovo [6]. Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 59 drones were destroyed approaching Moscow and reported no casualties or ground damage [6][5]. The outlet Astra said more than 460 flights had already been delayed or cancelled in Moscow and St Petersburg after the previous night's attack [7]. No Ukrainian military comment was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high that the airports were restricted, because Ukrainian and Russian outlets cite the same Russian aviation notices. Confidence is low on the interception count, which is the Russian mayor's own claim.

items.title: Ballistic Missiles Hit Warehouses on Kyiv's Left Bank, Killing One
items.lede: Shattered windows and burning debris also hit homes in the Ukrainian capital, hours after Zelensky warned that Moscow was preparing more ballistic attacks.

sections.text: Russia fired ballistic missiles at Kyiv, Ukraine's capital, on Thursday 29 October, minutes after an alert at 22:40 Kyiv time (21:40 CET), the Air Force and Mayor Vitali Klitschko said [8][9]. Klitschko said warehouse buildings in the Darnytskyi district were hit and set on fire, and that missile debris burned in a residential courtyard and partly destroyed a shop in the Dniprovskyi district [9][3]. The city military administration reported one person killed at 23:48 Kyiv time (22:48 CET) [9][8]. The BBC said monitors counted at least five to eight missiles [8]. Earlier that evening Zelensky said intelligence showed Russia preparing new ballistic strikes [10][8].

Confidence is high on the strike and the death, because the BBC, the Kyiv Independent, and Ukrinform carry the same on-record account from city officials. The missile count rests on monitoring channels cited by the BBC.

items.title: Ukraine's Navy Says Neptune Missile Destroyed Two Su-34 Bombers in Volgograd
items.lede: Ukrainian outlets put Moscow's remaining fleet of the guided-bomb carriers at about 140, and Ukrainska Pravda gives each an export value near 50 million dollars.

sections.text: Ukraine's Navy said on Thursday 29 October that a Neptune missile struck the Marinovka airfield near Oktyabrsky in Russia's Volgograd region, destroying two Su-34 fighter-bombers of the 11th Composite Aviation Regiment [11][12]. Ukrainska Pravda said a Long Neptune was used and put the export value of an Su-34 at about 50 million U.S. dollars [11]. The Navy said the Su-34 is one of Russia's main platforms for dropping guided bombs on Ukrainian cities and front-line positions [12][11]. Ukrinform and Ukrainska Pravda put Russia's remaining Su-34 fleet at about 140 aircraft as of October [12][11]. No Russian Defence Ministry comment was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high that Ukraine's Navy made the claim, because two Ukrainian outlets report its statement. Confidence is low on the damage, which rests on the Navy alone with no independent imagery read.

items.title: Injured Toll From Russia's Kremenchuk Strike Climbs to 28, Governor Says
items.lede: Children from a damaged boarding school reached a shelter in time, and an industrial site in the Ukrainian district was attacked early on Friday after ballistic missile warnings.

sections.text: A Russian drone struck an apartment building in Kremenchuk in Ukraine's Poltava region on Thursday 29 October, regional governor Vitalii Diakivnych and the State Emergency Service said [13][14]. Diakivnych said parked cars caught fire, that the injured count rose to 15 by 13:36 Kyiv time, and that the death toll rose to three at 13:53 Kyiv time (12:53 CET) [14]. Three children are among the injured [13]. By Thursday evening Diakivnych put the injured at 28, with 11 in hospital and one in critical condition, and said private homes and a boarding school were also damaged [15]. President Volodymyr Zelensky said six children and 26 adults were injured in the strike [16]. Early on Friday, after Air Force warnings of ballistic missiles heading for Kremenchuk, Diakivnych said an industrial enterprise in the Kremenchuk district was attacked, with details still being checked [17].

Confidence is high on the deaths and the rising injured count, because two Ukrainian outlets carry on-record figures from the governor; Zelensky's higher figure of 32 differs and was not reconciled. The overnight industrial strike rests on one outlet and has no damage details.

items.title: Aid Convoy for Ukraine's Occupied Oleshky Stands Ready After Routes Are Demined
items.lede: Residents wishing to leave have until 14:00 local time on Friday, with aid handouts due to start after 14:30, under a mission run jointly with Moscow's ombudsman.

sections.text: Ukraine and Russia have observed a ceasefire around Oleshky, a Russian-occupied town in Ukraine's Kherson region, since 03:00 Kyiv time on 27 October (02:00 CET) [18][19]. U.S. First Lady Melania Trump brokered the pause [20][21], and lawmaker David Arakhamia said it runs until 22:59 Kyiv time on 1 November [22]. The BBC said an estimated 1,700 to 2,000 people remain in Oleshky [23]. On Thursday evening Arakhamia said a joint Ukrainian, U.S., and Russian delegation had reached the point from which aid would be sent on Friday [24]. Ukraine's human rights commissioner Dmytro Lubinets said demining of the routes was complete, the convoy was ready to head for the central hospital, residents could leave until 14:00, and aid handouts would begin after 14:30 [25][26]. He said the mission is run jointly with Russia's ombudsman Yana Lantratova, who issued a similar statement [26][25]. Lubinets's office earlier said those leaving for Ukraine will travel through Russia and Belarus [27].

Confidence is high that the convoy was set to move on Friday, because Lubinets, Arakhamia, and Russia's ombudsman say so on record, reported by two Ukrainian outlets. The departure deadline rests on Lubinets alone.

items.title: Chernihiv Mourns Friday as Russia's Strike Leaves a Brother and Sister Critical
items.lede: Twenty-five people were hurt in the northern Ukrainian city, eight remain in hospital, and flags fly at half-mast for victims of nine days of attacks.

sections.text: A Russian drone struck the centre of Chernihiv in northern Ukraine on Thursday 29 October, setting shops and cars on fire, city military administration head Dmytro Bryzhynskyi and the city council said [28][29]. Regional governor Viacheslav Chaus said two 15-year-old girls were killed [28]. Police said as of 13:30 Kyiv time (12:30 CET) that 23 people were injured, among them a ten-month-old girl, a ten-year-old, and two teenagers aged 16 and 17 [29]. On Thursday evening Chaus put the injured at 25, including four children, and said a brother and sister were in critical condition, with eight people in hospital [30]. The city council declared Friday 30 October a day of mourning for residents killed by Russian strikes between 21 and 29 October [30]. Zelensky named the two girls as Yana and Mariia [16]. No Russian comment was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the deaths and the evening injured count, because two Ukrainian outlets and Zelensky's address carry on-record figures from city and regional officials.

items.title: Russian Jet Drone Kills 14 on a Crowded Platform at Ukraine's Dnipro Station
items.lede: Six of the wounded, among them an 11-year-old boy, are in serious condition, and Zelensky used the attack to demand fresh Western sanctions on Moscow.

sections.text: A Russian jet-powered drone hit a platform at the railway station in Dnipro, Ukraine, at about 11:00 Kyiv time (10:00 CET) on Thursday 29 October, where train No. 866 to Zaporizhzhia was standing [31][32]. Regional head Oleksandr Hanzha put the toll at 14 dead and 14 injured, six seriously, including an 11-year-old boy [31][33][34]. The Air Force said three of four jet drones aimed at the region were shot down [35][34]. Railway chief Oleksandr Pertsovskyi said many people were on the platform despite an elevated threat alert [32][33]. President Volodymyr Zelensky called for new EU, U.S., and G7 sanctions and said sanctions must not be eased while the war continues [36][34]. The BBC said Russia's military had not commented [33].
Confidence is high on the strike and the toll, because the BBC, DW, and two Ukrainian outlets carry the same on-record figures from regional, railway, and national officials.

items.title: Russia's Defence Ministry Claims 1,214 Ukrainian Drones Shot Down Overnight
items.lede: Kyiv's General Staff claimed hits on drone depots and two radars in Bryansk, while smoke rose over a defence-linked chemical plant in Bashkortostan.

sections.text: Russia's Defence Ministry said on Thursday 29 October that its air defences intercepted 1,214 Ukrainian drones overnight over regions including Bryansk, Belgorod, Kursk, Moscow, Bashkortostan, and Udmurtia [37][38]. Ukraine's General Staff said its forces hit a Geran drone store, a drone launch site, and a fuel depot near Navlya in Russia's Bryansk region, plus two radar stations near Starodub and Medvyodovo [39][40]. Monitoring channels and the outlet Astra reported a drone attack on Sterlitamak in Bashkortostan, with smoke near the Bashkir Soda Company chemical plant, which The Moscow Times said is on Russia's closed register of defence enterprises [41][42]. Sterlitamak's mayor, Emil Shaymardanov, said all eight drones over the city were shot down, that debris fell on an industrial plant causing minor damage, and that the plant was working normally [43].

Confidence is high that the ministry made the claim, because Interfax and Reuters report it. Confidence is low on the interception figure and the Ukrainian strike results rest on each side's own claims, and the extent of the Sterlitamak damage rests on the mayor's account and media reports.

items.title: Ukraine's Air Force Reports 112 Russian Drones Launched Into Thursday, 97 Stopped
items.lede: As of 08:00 Kyiv time on Thursday, hits were recorded at seven sites, 30 of 40 jet-powered Shaheds were stopped, and about seven drones were still airborne.

sections.text: Ukraine's Air Force said Russia launched 112 drones at Ukraine from 18:00 Kyiv time on 28 October (17:00 CET), Shaheds, 40 of them jet-powered, plus Gerbera attack drones and Parodiya decoys, from the directions of Oryol, Millerovo, and occupied Donetsk [44][45]. It said that as of 08:00 Kyiv time (07:00 CET) on Thursday 97 had been shot down or suppressed, including 30 jet-powered drones [44][45]. Hits were recorded at seven locations and falling debris at five, and about seven drones were still in the air [45].
Confidence is high on the figures, because two Ukrainian outlets carry the same on-record Air Force tally. The figures are the Air Force's own and were not independently checked.

theaters.heading: Sabotage, drones, cyber, disinformation, and espionage targeting European states

items.title: Bulgaria Asks Allies for More Support After Drones Sink the Contship Jet
items.lede: Prime Minister Radev says Sofia will summon the responsible ambassador once the drones' origin is proven, while Brussels calls the Black Sea attacks a dangerous escalation.

sections.text: Three maritime drones struck the container ship Contship Jet on Wednesday in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone, about 21 miles from Shabla, Defence Minister Dimitar Stoyanov said [1][2]. All 18 crew were rescued, and the ship sank; Bulgaria's Maritime Administration expected no significant harm to the sea or coast [3][4][5], and the navy commander said some containers fell overboard [6]. Reuters reported that at least six ships have been attacked off Bulgaria this month [5]. The Sofia Military District Prosecutor's Office opened pre-trial proceedings on Thursday under Article 415(1) of the Criminal Code, which covers prohibited methods of warfare, citing the attack on a ship flying the flag of neutral Liberia [7][8]. On Thursday evening, Prime Minister Rumen Radev said he had requested more allied support and that the relevant ambassador would be summoned once the drones' origin was established [9]. Defence chief Emil Eftimov said the drones stayed outside territorial waters, so were not engaged [9]. A European Commission spokesperson called the attacks a dangerous and unacceptable escalation arising from Russia's war against Ukraine [9]. No official attribution was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the strike, rescue, sinking, prosecutor's case, and statements, which BTA and other outlets carried. BTA and Reuters differ on this month's attack count.

items.title: Belgium's Finance Ministry Pulls Its MyMinfin Tax Portal Offline After a Cyberattack
items.lede: Officials say no taxpayer data leaked, filing deadlines move to 16 November, and federal police are investigating with no group yet named.

sections.text: Belgium's federal Finance Ministry (FOD Financiën) took MyMinfin, Tax-on-web, and Biztax offline after intruders penetrated its systems during the night from Tuesday to Wednesday, spokesman Francis Adyns said [10][11]. The outage was first reported on Wednesday evening [12]. The ministry said it detected the attack within a few hours, saw several attempts to alter parts of its digital environment, and contained the intrusion before attackers could take over applications or reach data [10][11]. It said there were no indications of a data breach and that the services must be rebuilt in an isolated environment, without giving a restoration date [10][11]. Tax returns due on 31 October can now be filed until 16 November [10][11]. Belgium's federal police and the Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium are investigating; no group has been named, and no claim of responsibility was found by the cutoff [10].
Confidence is high on the outage, the containment, and the deadline change, which the ministry stated on record and Belga and The Register carried. No attribution was found.

items.title: Danish Intelligence Warns Ukrainian Refugees Against Russian Sabotage Recruitment
items.lede: PET says Moscow could also aim to discredit refugees, with tasks disguised as journalism or market research and handlers hidden behind intermediaries.

sections.text: Denmark's Security and Intelligence Service (PET) on Thursday morning issued its sabotage-recruitment warning in Ukrainian, saying Russian intelligence services may try to use Ukrainian refugees in Denmark to prepare or carry out sabotage [13][14]. PET said Russia may also want to cast Ukrainian refugees in a bad light by making it look as if they back Russian sabotage [13][14]. Tasks such as photographing a company, checking access routes, or passing on harmless-seeming information can be disguised as journalism, market research, or documentation, and handlers may hide behind intermediaries [13][14]. Counter-espionage chief Emil Græsholm said the earlier warning to Danes now also had to reach Ukrainians [13]. PET says there is concrete Russian planning and preparation of sabotage in Denmark, an assessment Russia's embassy rejected in September [14].

Confidence is high that PET issued the warning and on its wording, which DR and Ritzau relayed from the press release. The PET release itself was not opened, and no new arrest or incident was announced.

theaters.heading: Politics, security, and defense across the EU and NATO's European members

items.title: Trappes Attack Suspect Charged With Terrorist Murder and Held in Custody
items.lede: The 39-year-old admits picking victims of Muslim or African appearance but denies terrorist intent, and police had released him after an assault days earlier.

sections.text: France's national anti-terrorism prosecutor's office (Pnat) said on Thursday that Kévin Tessier, 39, was charged with murder and attempted murders linked to a terrorist enterprise, aggravated by targeting victims over their real or supposed race, ethnicity, nation, or religion, franceinfo reported [1]. He was then remanded in custody, franceinfo learned from his lawyers and the Pnat [1][2]. Prosecutor Olivier Christen said the suspect admitted premeditation and specifically targeting people of Muslim, African, or North African appearance, but disputes any terrorist intent [1]. The attack in Trappes and La Verrière, in the Yvelines, killed Pengo Bossio Wangi, 26, and wounded seven, three of whom remain in hospital [1]. Police had arrested Tessier three days earlier for assaulting a Black man, then released him, a source close to the inquiry told franceinfo [1]. Trappes holds an anti-racism rally on Friday at 18:00 [1].

Confidence is high on the charges, custody, and the prosecutor's account, stated on record by the Pnat and reported by franceinfo and RTBF; the earlier arrest rests on one unnamed source cited by franceinfo.

items.title: Italian Chinook Flying for EU Force Crashes in Bosnia, Killing Four
items.lede: Two soldiers and two Red Cross military volunteers died, Rome says, and the 11 injured are out of danger as investigators look for a cause.

sections.text: An Italian CH-47 Chinook flying for the EU peacekeeping force EUFOR Althea crashed at about 16:00 on Thursday near Brčko in north-eastern Bosnia and Herzegovina, close to the Croatian border, NOS reported, citing Italy's defence ministry [3]. EUFOR said the aircraft came down during a routine operation at Gorica, with no civilians hurt [4]. Fifteen people were on board; three died at the scene and a fourth in Brčko hospital, the hospital said [4]. Italy's Defence Minister Guido Crosetto said the dead were two Italian Army soldiers and two members of the Italian Red Cross Military Volunteer Corps, and that none of the 11 injured was in danger of death [5]. Italy sent a military medical team [5]. The cause is under investigation [3]. Dutch troops also serve in the mission, NOS noted [3].

Confidence is high on the toll, the aircraft, and the victims' units, stated by EUFOR, the hospital, and Italy's defence ministry and reported by ANSA, franceinfo, and NOS. No cause had been given by the cutoff.

items.title: Judges Spare Presidential Hopeful Édouard Philippe Charges in Le Havre Funds Case
items.lede: Assisted-witness status, a step short of formal charges, eases the legal threat to his 2027 run, though the whistleblower's lawyer says the inquiry goes on.

sections.text: Former French Prime Minister Édouard Philippe, the Horizons party's presidential candidate, was placed under assisted-witness status on Thursday after a full day before two financial investigating judges, AFP learned from sources including his lawyer, franceinfo and RTBF reported [6][7]. The inquiry covers suspected misuse of public funds, favouritism, and workplace harassment at the Le Havre urban community, where he is mayor [6]. The status is less incriminating than being formally charged and can change if new evidence emerges [6]. His lawyer, Emmanuel Marsigny, said the decision confirms there is nothing to reproach him for [6][7]. The case began with a 2023 complaint by whistleblower Cornelia Findeisen, a former deputy director-general there; her lawyer, Jérôme Karsenti, said the investigation continues [6][7].
Confidence is high on the status and the lawyers' statements, reported by franceinfo and RTBF from AFP sourcing; no statement from the judges or the financial prosecutor was found by the cutoff.

items.title: Spain's Rail Investigators Put Urda Crash Toll at 74, Above the 69 Bodies Recovered
items.lede: Unions and Vox are turning on Transport Minister Óscar Puente after leaked control-centre audio, a month before the 29 November snap election.

sections.text: Spain's state-run Renfe AVE high-speed train ran into the back of a stationary private Iryo train on the Madrid–Andalusia line in Toledo province at about 08:53 on Wednesday, El País reported [8][9]. Transport Minister Óscar Puente said the LZB signalling system failed at about 08:30, halting six trains, and that the Adif control centre ordered them at about 08:36 to resume normal running, calling the decision inexplicable [8][9]. The rail accident investigation commission, CIAF, put the toll at 74 in a preliminary report on Thursday evening, while sources at the forward command post said 69 bodies had been recovered, RTBF reported [10]. The BBC, using 69, said more than 100 people were injured and named victims including former employment minister Fátima Báñez [11]. The SEMAF drivers' union called the leak of control-centre audio alarming, and the CCOO union demanded Puente's resignation; Vox filed a Supreme Court complaint against him [10]. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez declared three days of mourning [12][13]. Puente is due to give a press conference on Friday morning [10].

Confidence is high on the crash, the mourning, and the union and party statements; confidence is moderate on the toll, since the investigation commission's 74 and the command post's 69 conflict and no reconciled figure was found by the cutoff.

items.title: Von der Leyen Keeps Pitching Associate Membership to Canada at Montreal Summit
items.lede: Germany and other EU states had the term struck from the draft statement, while Ottawa says the label matters less than the ties themselves.

sections.text: The European Union has dropped Commission President Ursula von der Leyen's offer of associate membership talks for Canada from the draft statement for the EU–Canada summit in Montreal on Thursday and Friday, El País and the Guardian reported [14][15]. EU ambassadors raised legal and political concerns on Monday; Italy proposed keeping the Commission's wording, while Germany pushed the softer formula, the Guardian reported [15]. At the summit on Thursday, von der Leyen still described associate membership as a partnership closer to membership than anything the EU has done before, open only to its closest partners outside Europe, the BBC reported [16]. Germany's ambassador to Canada said the term is used for Ukraine and Moldova [16]. At a business roundtable on Thursday, Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada and the EU were forging an "alliance for the future, with Canada as an associate member", after telling reporters earlier that the name "doesn't matter" [17]. The joint statement is due at the close of the summit on Friday and had not been published by the cutoff.

Confidence is high that the wording was dropped from the draft and on von der Leyen's remarks, reported by El País, the Guardian, and the BBC; the member-state positions rest on unnamed diplomatic sourcing.

items.title: France Deploys 70,000 Police for Saturday's Protests and Bans Halloween-Night Gatherings
items.lede: Nuñez promised extreme firmness and tighter checks than on 24 October, while the casseurs-payeurs bill and riot surcharge are still pending.

sections.text: France's Senate adopted the casseurs-payeurs bill on Wednesday by 229 votes to 105, making violent groups jointly liable for damage [18]. Arrests in the 24 October marches reached 1,314, with 53 officers injured [19][20]. In Reims, the police watchdog IGPN was tasked with investigating after a police grenade seriously injured a marcher's shin, franceinfo reported [21]. Franceinfo reported a planned compulsory 0.8 per cent riot insurance surcharge from 1 January 2027, which the Conseil d'État must still validate [22]. On Wednesday evening President Emmanuel Macron called for calm, conceding the response had been too slow [23]. On Thursday, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez wrote to prefects that the risk of urban violence on Saturday is very high [24]. On Thursday evening he announced 70,000 police and gendarmes for 31 October, the same as a week earlier, backed by elite units, drones, and 26 Centaure armoured vehicles [25]. Prefects will keep marches out of city centres, and Halloween-night gatherings called online will be banned and dispersed, he said [25]. Lorient prosecutors opened an inquiry into masked shop-defence patrols seen during the 24 October march [26].
Confidence is high on the deployment, the bans, and the vote, stated on record and reported by franceinfo, with AFP, and Public Sénat. No new baton charges were reported by the cutoff.

items.title: ECB President Lagarde Will Step Down in February, Nine Months Early
items.lede: EU leaders have started choosing her successor immediately, and the euro-area bank held its deposit rate at 2.5 per cent the same day.

sections.text: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde told the Governing Council in Frankfurt, Germany, and European Council President António Costa on Thursday that she will leave on 7 February 2027, the ECB said [27]. Franceinfo, citing AFP, put the departure nearly nine months before her term ends [28]. Costa said the process to appoint her successor under Article 283 of the EU treaty began the same day, with a decision by euro-area leaders [29]. At its meeting the same day, the ECB left rates unchanged, with the deposit rate at 2.50 per cent, the main refinancing rate at 2.65 per cent, and the marginal lending rate at 2.90 per cent [30][28]. The bank said financing conditions had tightened since September, after two rate rises this year driven by energy prices [28]. No reason for the early exit was given in the ECB statement.
Confidence is high on the departure date and the rate decision, stated by the ECB and the European Council and reported by ANSA and franceinfo.

theaters.heading: Security, politics, and Russian pressure on Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania

items.title: Estonia Has Finished Only 28 of Nearly 600 Planned Border Bunkers
items.lede: Procurement disputes delayed the work, but the defence investment centre still aims to finish the roughly €60 million defence zone by the end of 2027.

sections.text: Estonia has completed the first concrete bunkers of the Baltic Defence Line near Narva, but only 28 of the nearly 600 required along its eastern border are ready, ERR's Aktuaalne kaamera reported on Thursday [1]. Armin Siilivask, the Estonian Centre for Defence Investment's project manager for the line, said work on further strongpoints had been due to start in the third quarter but was held up by procurement disputes that have now been resolved [1]. The Estonian section runs about 100 kilometres, and thousands of concrete "dragon's teeth" are stockpiled along the border for rapid placement [1]. Defence Forces engineer inspector Ainar Afanasjev said Estonia has no ground to give up to buy time, so defence starts at the border [1]. The zone is costed at nearly €60 million, nearly 600 bunkers are due by the end of 2027, and the Centre for Defence Investment hopes to finish on schedule [1]. No Defence Ministry statement was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the figures rest on one ERR television report quoting officials on record.

items.title: Riigikogu Anti-Corruption Panel Probes Estonia's €200 Million Turkish Armoured Vehicle Deal
items.lede: Critics say the 230 Otokar and Nurol Makina vehicles do not fit neighbours' equipment, while Defence Minister Herem defends the price and delivery speed.

sections.text: The Estonian parliament's anti-corruption select committee is examining why the Centre for Defence Investment bought wheeled armoured vehicles from Turkey, ERR reported on Thursday [2]. Estonia bought 230 vehicles from Otokar and Nurol Makina for about €200 million a few years ago, and all have been delivered [2]. Experts in a Riigikogu defence committee report say the deal abandoned strategic cooperation with neighbours and left equipment incompatible with theirs in wartime [2]. Retired Major General Meelis Kiili, a committee member, questioned the move to a distant supplier ecosystem [2]. Defence Minister Martin Herem said price and delivery speed decided the purchase and that spare parts supply has had no problems so far [2]. The Centre for Defence Investment declined to comment [2].
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on one ERR report with the minister and committee member on record; the committee report was not read.

items.title: Latvia Keeps Digging Anti-Tank Ditches on Its Belarus Border Through Winter
items.lede: Only the first six kilometres are dug so far, and builders aim to finish a 27-kilometre opening stretch of the Baltic Defence Line by spring.

sections.text: Latvia has dug the first six kilometres of anti-tank ditches in its eastern border municipalities and plans to keep working through the winter, Latvian public media's Latgale bureau reported on Thursday [3]. Digging on the Latvia–Belarus border in Augšdaugava municipality began in September, including on land expropriated from residents [3]. Dace Plotniece of the state property company VNĪ said work sped up as more forest was cleared [3]. Lieutenant Colonel Pēteris Suveizda, commander of the National Guard's 3rd Latgale Brigade, said obstacles go only where terrain offers mobility corridors, not along the whole border, and that barbed wire and minefields would be added in a crisis [3]. Soil conditions and access roads are complicating the work [3].
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on one LSM report quoting officials on record.

items.title: Saeima Lets Latvian Border Guards Fire Without Warning to Repel Attacks
items.lede: Lawmakers framed the amendments as a response to hybrid warfare on the eastern frontier, and any death or injury must reach prosecutors within 24 hours.

sections.text: Latvia's Saeima on Thursday adopted amendments to the State Border Guard Law and the Criminal Procedure Law giving border guards explicit rights to use physical force, combat techniques, weapons, and dogs to repel attacks on people or border infrastructure, LSM reported [4]. A weapon may be used without warning when a warning is not possible, and any injury or death from its use must be reported to prosecutors within 24 hours [4]. The law previously did not spell out such rights [4]. Defence Committee chair Raimonds Bergmanis said a hybrid war is under way at Latvia's external border [4]. Offences by border guards under the enhanced border regime will be investigated by the State Border Guard's own officials [4]. No statement from the State Border Guard was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the vote rests on one LSM report; the adopted text was not read.

items.title: EU Commission Turns Down Baltic States' €500 Million Anti-Drone Funding Request
items.lede: Defence Commissioner Kubilius points Lithuania, Latvia, and Estonia instead to SAFE defence loans; the Commission opened a second €21.3 billion SAFE call on Thursday, with counter-drone systems among its priorities.

sections.text: The European Commission has answered a late-September letter from the defence ministers of Lithuania, Latvia, and Estonia seeking €500 million for anti-drone defences, but offered no new funding on that scale, LRT reported on Thursday [5]. Commissioner Andrius Kubilius told LRT on Wednesday that one option is the SAFE loan instrument, with a new call coming soon because €21 billion remained after the first round [5]. He said few other large EU budget sources exist as the budget period nears its end [5]. On Thursday the Commission invited all member states into a second SAFE round worth €21.3 billion, naming air and missile defence, drones, and counter-drone systems among the priorities [6]. Lithuanian Defence Minister Robertas Kaunas said the three states wanted to combine drone detection, artificial intelligence, and interception into an integrated air defence system [5]. ELTA, via tv3.lt, reported the Commission's answer, and President Gitanas Nausėda said on Thursday that Lithuania will consider SAFE loans while defence purchases stay funded from the state budget [7]. ERR carried LRT's account [8]. No written Commission statement was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high that the request was turned down, reported by LRT and ELTA with Kubilius and Nausėda on record; the Commission's reply letter was not read.

items.title: Zelenskyy Wants to Attend Ukraine Recovery Conference in Estonia, Tsahkna Says
items.lede: Invitations to world leaders for the 28–29 January Tallinn meeting are signed, though the foreign minister says attendance depends on wartime conditions in January.

sections.text: Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said at the government's weekly press conference on Thursday that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy wants to attend the Ukraine Recovery Conference in Tallinn, ERR reported [9]. He said Zelenskyy and Prime Minister Kristen Michal have signed personal invitations to leaders, and the event will be held at world-leader level [9]. Tsahkna said attendance depends on the situation in Ukraine in January, after media speculation that a hard winter could keep Kyiv's leadership away [9]. He said the aim is billions in additional funding for Ukraine [9]. The conference is set for 28 and 29 January [9]. No Ukrainian presidential office statement was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the remarks rest on one ERR report of an on-record press conference; Kyiv's side was not read.

items.title: Latvia's President Will Ask Kulbergs on 4 November to Form a Government
items.lede: Rinkēvičs says he is confident a cabinet will emerge, while United List is reported to want Edvards Smiltēns as speaker of the new Saeima.

sections.text: Latvian President Edgars Rinkēvičs said on Latvian Radio on Thursday that on the morning of 4 November he will sign an order inviting Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs of the United List to form the next cabinet, giving him legal standing to proceed [10]. Rinkēvičs called the situation not ordinary but said he was confident a government would be formed and that the rest is up to the parties [10]. The newly elected Saeima first meets on 3 November [10]. United List holds 41 seats, enough for a minimal majority with the National Alliance's ten, or a broader one adding New Unity's seven [10]. Kulbergs opened formal coalition talks on Wednesday [11]. Latvian Television reported on Wednesday that United List plans to put Edvards Smiltēns forward as speaker and former president Raimonds Vējonis as a deputy speaker, leaving New Unity without a presidium post [12]. No United List statement confirming the presidium plan was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the nomination date, stated by the president on Latvian Radio; confidence is moderate on the presidium plan, which rests on one LTV report citing unnamed information.

items.title: Lithuania Sets 2032 Start for Universal Military Conscription
items.lede: The annual intake would rise from just over 5,000 to about 7,500 young people, after the military asked for time to train instructors and build barracks.

sections.text: Lithuania's State Defence Council agreed on Thursday to introduce universal military conscription in 2032, President Gitanas Nausėda told reporters after the meeting, BNS reported via LRT [13]. Women would still serve only voluntarily [13]. Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius said the government wanted a faster transition but the military said it would be ready by 2032 [13]. Preparations include training about 300 instructors and building housing for draftees [13]. The council also agreed to widen service options, such as drone operator training and support to the border guard and rescue services [13]. Lithuania restored partial conscription in 2015 [13]. No published council decision text was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the decision rests on one BNS report via LRT quoting the president and prime minister on record.

items.title: Lithuania Charges Two Germany-Based Men With Terrorism Over Starlink Arson Attempt
items.lede: The dual nationals in their 20s were already held in Germany at Bulgaria's request, and investigators tie them to similar attacks in Poland and Bulgaria.

sections.text: Lithuanian law enforcement said on Thursday that two men in their 20s suspected of trying to set fire to Starlink equipment in Vilnius earlier this month have been arrested in Germany at Bulgaria's request [14]. One holds German and Turkish citizenship and the other German and Serbian, Saulius Briginas of the Lithuanian Criminal Police Bureau said [14]. He said the men arrived the day before, left right after, and had prepared in advance [14]. Prosecutor Nėrijus Puškorius said they are suspected of terrorist offences; a transfer decision comes later [14]. Reuters, citing the Prosecutor General's Office, reported that both were charged and that Lithuania treats the 18 October attempt as Russia-linked sabotage aimed at Ukraine's military capabilities [15]. Investigators link them to Starlink arson cases in Poland and Bulgaria [14]. The target was premises of Lithuanian firm Delska, where SpaceX stores Starlink gear [14]. Moscow has called such accusations baseless [15]. No German authority statement was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the arrests and charges, reported by BNS via LRT and Reuters from Lithuanian police and prosecutors on record; the Russia link is Lithuania's assessment; no German source was read.

items.title: Lithuania Weighs Palantir Battlefield Software for Its Armed Forces
items.lede: TV3 puts the first seven years of use at nearly €200 million, and Defence Minister Kaunas says planned spending may need shifting to pay for it.

sections.text: Lithuania's Defence Minister Robertas Kaunas told TV3 News on Wednesday that the country is considering buying an artificial intelligence system from US company Palantir for its armed forces, BNS reported via LRT on Thursday [16]. He said the system would integrate large volumes of data and support battlefield decision-making, and that NATO countries need such software [16]. TV3 reported the first seven years would cost nearly €200 million, possibly more [16]. Kaunas said some reallocation of funds may be needed because the final price is not yet known [16]. No Palantir statement was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the minister's remarks rest on one BNS report via LRT; the cost figure is TV3's and was not read directly.

items.title: Serbia's Student List Demands Police, Intelligence, and Prosecution Chiefs Quit
items.lede: Newly elected MPs fear evidence of wrongdoing could vanish during a handover that will take weeks, so they want heads to roll now.

sections.text: Serbia's Student List, which is set to hold around 140 of the National Assembly's 250 seats after the 25 October election, on Thursday demanded the resignation of top police, intelligence, and judicial officials at a press conference in Pioneers' Park opposite parliament [1] [2]. Candidate Svetlana Stanarević named police director Dragan Vasiljević, gendarmerie commander Radoslav Repac, and anti-terror unit commander Igor Žmirić, and the movement also wants BIA director Vladimir Orlić and military intelligence chief Đuro Jovanić out [2]. Candidate Jovan Vujičić sought the departure of Belgrade's higher public prosecutor Nenad Stefanović and Constitutional Court president Vladan Petrov [2]. The list also demanded the resignation of Telekom Srbija chief Vladimir Lučić [2]. The BBC said the handover of power will take weeks and the movement worries evidence could be destroyed meanwhile [1]. The new majority will not be verified for at least another month, and most media remain under the influence of Aleksandar Vučić and his allies [3]. Preliminary results from 8,338 of 8,392 polling stations give the Student List 53.04 percent and Vučić's list 38.97 percent [2]. No resignation by any named official was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the demands, reported by the BBC and RTS; the seat count and results remain preliminary.

items.title: Serbia's RTS Purges News Editors as Students Reject On-Air Apology
items.lede: Deputy Dejan Jovanović now runs the broadcaster in an acting capacity, but the Student List wants him gone too, saying only resignations will do.

sections.text: Manja Grcic, director-general of Serbia's public broadcaster RTS, resigned on Wednesday evening, a day after ruling out stepping down, after the Student List demanded that RTS management and news editors resign [4]. Her deputy Dejan Jovanović became acting director-general, and longtime Dnevnik editor Borivoje Uskoković was named acting head of the news programme, Gledaj.rs reported [5]. Uskoković then removed the editors of the correspondents', regional, Oko, website, and diaspora sections, plus three editors of the 19:30 Dnevnik, according to RTS's website [5]. On Thursday the main evening news was briefly delayed by a false bomb threat, and a statement from the new news leadership was read on air as a "first measure of apology" [5]. Students in blockade replied that they accept "only resignations" [5]. At a press conference on Thursday, Student List candidate Mirjana Nikolić said the movement still wants Jovanović to resign over selective reporting, RTS reported [2]. No response from Jovanović was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the staff changes rest on Gledaj.rs citing RTS's website, and the Student List's demand on Jovanović on RTS itself; the bomb threat was not confirmed by police.

items.title: Bulgaria's Run-Off Rivals Split Over Russia in Their Only TV Debate
items.lede: Yotova pitched a Black Sea ceasefire talk including Moscow, while Gyurov called that wishful thinking and pressed for drone defences ahead of Sunday's vote.

sections.text: Bulgaria's acting President Iliana Yotova and former caretaker premier Andrey Gyurov met on Thursday evening on BNT in the only televised debate before Sunday's 1 November run-off, after a first round in which Yotova took 34.76 percent and Gyurov 31.95 percent [6] [7]. Yotova proposed a meeting of the six Black Sea states, Russia included, to agree a moratorium on hostilities after drones hit merchant ships in Bulgaria's economic zone [6] [8]. Gyurov answered that "a moratorium, expressed merely as a wish, does not constitute a defense strategy. Silence is not defense," and urged Bulgaria to join European drone and missile defence efforts [8] [6]. Yotova said peace can come only through negotiations and that Russia cannot be excluded [6]. Asked whether she would uphold the government's policies as president, Yotova did not answer, while Gyurov called himself an independent candidate [6]. Earlier, the election commission cleared Prime Minister Rumen Radev of breaching the electoral code by 8 votes to 7 and referred complaints about official channels to the National Audit Office; Gyurov's committee appealed to the Supreme Administrative Court [9] [10]. No court ruling on the appeal was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the debate exchanges, reported by Novinite and BGNES; the first-round figures and commission ruling come from BNT and BTA.

items.title: Kosovo Suspends Peja's Top Prosecutors and 11 Police Officers Over Femicide
items.lede: The move follows BIRN's finding that Arlinda Zekaj told police her brother-in-law, now accused of the axe killing, had threatened her life three days earlier.

sections.text: Kosovo's Prosecutorial Council on Thursday suspended Peja chief prosecutor Lumturije Vucetaj and her deputy Arlinda Nallbani Gacaferri, who coordinated domestic-violence cases, council member Dardan Vuniqi told BIRN [11]. Kosovo Police suspended 11 officers in the Peja region at the Police Inspectorate's request, including the regional director, a station commander, and the head of investigations [11]. Zekaj was killed on Sunday evening in Vitomirica near Peja after police accompanied her home, and a judge had let her and her ex-husband keep sharing a house two metres apart [12]. Her brother-in-law Albert Sylaj was remanded for 30 days on Wednesday on suspicion of the killing; her ex-husband Jeton Sylaj was remanded on Tuesday for violating a court order [11]. Hundreds marched in Pristina on Wednesday demanding that Justice Minister Donika Gervalla and Interior Minister Xhelal Svecla resign [12]. Prime Minister Albin Kurti blamed the judiciary at a government meeting on Wednesday [12]. Activists said protests would continue on Thursday [11]. No ministerial response to the resignation calls was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the suspensions, remands, and protests rest on BIRN reporting alone, though it quotes a named council member.

items.title: North Macedonia Treads Carefully on Bulgaria Dispute During Sofia's Election Race
items.lede: North Macedonia's foreign minister said no meeting with his Bulgarian counterpart is planned before December's NATO and OSCE gatherings, while Slovakia pledged strong support for Skopje's EU bid.

sections.text: North Macedonia's Foreign Minister Timco Mucunski said on Thursday in Skopje that his government was in dialogue with Bulgaria, the EU institutions, and all member states on unblocking its EU accession, but would be cautious so as not to become part of Bulgaria's presidential campaign [13] [14]. He spoke at a joint press conference with visiting Slovak Foreign Minister Juraj Blanar [13]. Mucunski said he could meet Bulgarian Foreign Minister Velislava Petrova on the sidelines of NATO and OSCE meetings in December and sought a long-term agreement rather than a temporary fix [13]. Asked about the case of Iva Mihailova, he said it was indecent for a European Union member state to become a refuge for people convicted of crimes or facing court proceedings [14] [15]. He said he had recently presented Skopje's position to France's minister for European affairs in Montenegro [13]. Blanar said North Macedonia could count on Slovakia's strong support [13]. No Bulgarian government response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the press-conference remarks, reported by BTA and Albeu; the refuge remark is carried by Albeu and Bulgarian outlets.

items.title: Azerbaijani Premier Ali Asadov Lands in Tbilisi for Economic Commission Talks
items.lede: Four Azerbaijani ministers travel with him, and Georgia's economy minister flagged energy, transport, and Middle Corridor projects for the two-day meeting.

sections.text: Azerbaijan's Prime Minister Ali Asadov arrived in Georgia on Thursday for a working visit on 29–30 October and was met at Tbilisi airport by Deputy Prime Minister and Economy Minister Mariam Kvrivishvili, Interpressnews reported [1]. The two prime ministers co-chair the 11th meeting of the intergovernmental commission on economic cooperation, and Asadov is to hold a one-on-one meeting with Georgian Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze, according to the Georgian government's administration [2]. His delegation includes Azerbaijan's ministers of economy, energy, digital development and transport, and science and education [2]. Kvrivishvili said the talks would cover energy, transport, investment, and trade, and regional projects in the Middle Corridor [1]. No outcome of the commission or the Kobakhidze meeting was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the visit rests on Interpressnews reports relaying Georgian government statements; no Azerbaijani source was read.

items.title: Georgian Appeals Court Frees Journalist Held on Treason Charge on Bail
items.lede: Dito Chubinidze walked out after paying 4,000 lari, crediting pressure from abroad, and still faces up to four years in prison if convicted.

sections.text: The Tbilisi Court of Appeals in Georgia on Thursday released Asaval-Dasavali journalist Dito Chubinidze on bail of GEL 4,000 (about USD 1,550), Civil.ge reported [3]. He was arrested on 22 October after the Prosecutor General's Office accused him of deliberately spreading false claims that Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze had secretly agreed to hand parts of the Davit Gareji monastery complex to Azerbaijan [3]. Prosecutors charged him with treason, specifically sabotage, saying his reports had damaged the work of the Georgian-Azerbaijani border commission; he denies it and faces up to four years in prison if convicted [3]. After his release Chubinidze thanked his lawyer, Georgian society, and supporters abroad, and said he would have refused a plea deal and gone to the European Court of Human Rights if needed [3]. The Media Advocacy Coalition had warned that the case set a dangerous precedent for press freedom [3]. No prosecution comment on the bail ruling was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the release and quotes rest on Civil.ge; an Interpressnews headline reports the same bail sum but was not opened.

items.title: Armenia's Deputy Speaker Hurls Chair as Parliament Brawl Leaves MPs Hurt
items.lede: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan backed his party's MPs and warned that violent opponents would have their arms broken, drawing a rebuke from the human rights ombudsman.

sections.text: A brawl broke out in Armenia's parliament on Thursday between MPs of the ruling Civil Contract party and the opposition Strong Armenia faction, OC Media reported [4]. It began when Civil Contract MP Taron Chakhoyan accused the opposition of corruption and mocked Strong Armenia leader Narek Karapetyan's family [4]. Deputy Speaker Vahagn Aleksanyan threw a chair towards opposition MPs, bottles were thrown, and MPs left with injuries and torn clothing; Speaker Ruben Rubinyan called a recess of about an hour [4]. Citing RFE/RL, OC Media said the fight continued in the corridors until security staff separated the sides [4]. Rubinyan blamed Karapetyan for starting it, and Pashinyan said "whether with a chair or something else, it is proportionate and right" [4]. Ombudsman Anahit Manasyan said the incident must be investigated under the law [4]. JAMnews, reporting the same livestreamed scenes, quoted Pashinyan as saying the authorities would "break the arms" of anyone who tries to use violence, and Manasyan as warning that such incidents feed public acceptance of violence [5]. No count of injured MPs was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the brawl and Pashinyan's backing, reported by OC Media and JAMnews from the official livestream; the injuries are not quantified.

items.title: Georgian Opposition Turns Party-Ban Test Against Georgian Dream in Court
items.lede: Council of Europe chief Alain Berset warned that a ban needs a strong legal basis and could reach the Strasbourg court, with hearings scheduled to run to 30 October.

sections.text: Georgia's Constitutional Court began substantive hearings on Monday on a lawsuit by 88 Georgian Dream MPs to declare five opposition parties unconstitutional: Unity – National Movement, Coalition for Change, Lelo – Strong Georgia, Gakharia for Georgia, and the Federalists [6]. On the sixth day, Court President Revaz Nadaraia twice cut off coalition lawyers, ruling a European Parliament resolution irrelevant and calling coalition lawyer Giga Lemonjava's argument that the suit echoes Russia's account of the 2008 war "demagoguery" [7]. Hearings are scheduled to continue through 30 October, and a ruling is due by 24 June 2027 [7]. On Thursday coalition lawyer Nika Gvaramia argued that, by the lawsuit's own standard, Georgian Dream itself should be banned [8]. Asked by Gvaramia whether corrupt judges should go, Nadaraia said he knew of none and told him to respect the court [9]. Council of Europe Secretary General Alain Berset said in Strasbourg on 27 October that a ban needs a strong legal basis and the case could reach the European Court of Human Rights, JAMnews reported on Thursday [10].
Confidence is high on the court's earlier rulings, reported by JAMnews and The Messenger; Thursday's exchanges rest on Genews and Interpressnews, and Berset's remarks on JAMnews alone.

items.title: Moscow Forum Launches Foundation to Restore Georgia–Russia Diplomatic Ties
items.lede: Its co-founders include fugitive former prosecutor general Otar Partskhaladze, who is sanctioned by the US and UK and wanted by Georgian authorities.

sections.text: A forum in Moscow on Wednesday proposed a Russian-Georgian university, wider teaching of Russian in Georgia, and restored services at Lomisi Church as steps towards renewing diplomatic relations, which Georgia and Russia cut after the 2008 war, OC Media reported on Thursday [11]. Participants set up a foundation called Unity of Russians and Georgians, co-founded by Partskhaladze, Moscow-based businessman Mamuka Pipia of the pro-Russian Solidarity for Peace party, and Davit Tsetskhladze of the Russian-Georgian Business Council [11]. Russian Foreign Ministry official Vasily Gavrilov attended and said better relations served both countries [11]. The Russian Interests Section at the Swiss Embassy in Tbilisi said the event aimed to promote restored relations and called on President Vladimir Putin and Georgia's government to back closer ties [11]. The forum came a week after Georgia named First Deputy Foreign Minister Giorgi Zurabashvili the prime minister's special representative for relations with Russia [11]. No Georgian government comment on the forum was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on one OC Media report drawing partly on Sputnik Georgia footage; no second outlet was read.

items.title: Pashinyan Says Armenia May Avoid Snap Elections Over a New Constitution
items.lede: Justice Minister Srbuhi Galyan said a draft charter will be ready in mid-November, and Pashinyan hopes to make a referendum offer the opposition cannot refuse, though he gave no guarantee.

sections.text: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan told a press briefing on Thursday there was a high probability that the matter would not reach snap parliamentary elections [12]. He had earlier floated early elections to win the constitutional majority his Civil Contract party needs for constitutional change, which Azerbaijan demands as a precondition for a peace deal [13]. Pashinyan said Wednesday's government question session in parliament made it possible to build strong public pressure on the opposition to allow, with its votes, a referendum on a new constitution, though he could not guarantee he would be able to formulate that proposal [12]. Justice Minister Srbuhi Galyan told Factor.am the draft would be ready in mid-November and discussed at length, and called snap elections "one of the very good options" that had not been decided [14]. Galyan told reporters the government's agenda was to write a new constitution, not to remove anything from the current one, when asked about Baku's demand to drop the reference to Armenia's Declaration of Independence [15]. No response from the Strong Armenia opposition faction was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: Pashinyan's and Galyan's remarks rest on NEWS.am reports, one relayed from Factor.am; OC Media supplies only the background.

items.title: CDU Deputy Leader Prien Calls for Taxing Revenue Generated by Artificial Intelligence
items.lede: The idea splits Merz's own cabinet: his economy minister wants AI rolled out first, and the digital minister has already backed away from it.

sections.text: Germany's family minister and CDU deputy leader Karin Prien told Stern that if value creation runs mainly through artificial intelligence, it must be taxed, adding that there was no other way [1] [2]. She also said Germany must dare to scale back the welfare state and invest more in children and young people [1]. Digital Minister Karsten Wildberger (CDU) had backed such a tax in the Tagesspiegel but later retreated, saying growth should come first, while Economy Minister Katherina Reiche (CDU) said AI should be introduced before it is taxed [2] [1]. Chancellor Friedrich Merz has so far been critical of an AI tax [2] [1]. The SPD's Bundestag group called in September for fair taxation of profits, but the coalition has no concrete plans [2].
Confidence is high that Prien made the remarks and on the cabinet split, reported by Stern, which conducted the interview, and by tagesschau with ARD's Berlin studio.

items.title: Steinmeier Urges China at Peking University to Press Russia Into Serious Negotiations
items.lede: Germany's head of state paired the Ukraine appeal with a demand for fair trade, warning Beijing against flooding Europe with subsidised exports before Friday's Xi meeting.

sections.text: Germany's Federal President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, on a state visit to China, used a speech at Peking University, which made him an honorary professor, to say the international order is under attack as never before [3] [4] [5]. He said China, a permanent Security Council member with close ties to Moscow, should work with Germany so that Russia stops its attacks and enters serious negotiations [3]. On trade, he said Europe wants no decoupling but cannot accept restricted access to China's market while subsidised Chinese exports flood European markets, and he called Beijing's pledge to export fewer hybrid cars encouraging [3]. With size and power comes great responsibility, he said [3] [5]. He is due to meet President Xi Jinping on Friday [3]. No Chinese government response to the speech was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the speech's content, reported by tagesschau and Deutschlandfunk and posted on the Federal President's website.

items.title: Volkswagen Posts a 5.8 Billion Euro Third-Quarter Loss on a Porsche Write-Down
items.lede: The red ink deepens pressure on German jobs: a further 50,000 cuts are already planned worldwide, and closing domestic plants is under discussion.

sections.text: Germany's largest carmaker, Volkswagen, reported an after-tax loss of 5.82 billion euros for July to September, against a loss of 1.07 billion euros a year earlier [6] [7]. Special items of 7.8 billion euros in the quarter drove the result, chiefly a non-cash 6.4 billion euro impairment of Porsche goodwill, about one billion euros of impairments on Chinese assets, and costs tied to the planned sale of its Osnabrück plant [6]. Quarterly revenue fell 6.3 per cent to about 75.3 billion euros, deliveries fell 14.3 per cent to 1.89 million vehicles, and sales in China dropped 38.5 per cent [7] [6]. Finance chief Arno Antlitz said the group must act quickly and decisively and cited US tariffs, a shrinking Chinese market, and lower earnings on electric cars [6]. The group still expects an operating margin of up to one per cent for 2026 [6]. Its supervisory board decided in September to cut a further 50,000 jobs worldwide, and plant closures in Germany are under discussion, Deutschlandfunk reported [8].
Confidence is high on the figures, stated in Volkswagen's own release and reported by ZDFheute via dpa and by Deutschlandfunk.

items.title: Baden-Württemberg Interior Minister Hagel Warns Stone-Throwers Ahead of Saturday Youth Rallies
items.lede: A Stuttgart organiser now calls France's unrest a model, while pupil representatives nationwide are distancing themselves partly over fear of violence.

sections.text: Rallies by the 'Gen Z regelt' or 'Gen Z steht auf' initiative are planned in about 30 German cities on Saturday, tagesschau reported [9] [10]. Baden-Württemberg Interior Minister Manuel Hagel (CDU) told the Mannheimer Morgen that peaceful protesters are protected by the Basic Law and the police, but whoever throws stones loses both [11]. He defended his earlier 'violent mob' remark, saying it meant those planning to bring violence from the neighbouring country, where he said 2,400 people were arrested in a single day and 150 police officers injured [11]. In Stuttgart, where several thousand marchers are expected, a 19-year-old local organiser told the Stuttgarter Zeitung that the French protests are a model and the city should brace itself, while rejecting vandalism of private property [12] [13]. The paper says the domestic intelligence service is watching her group, the Internationale Jugend [12]. The Federal Students' Conference and numerous pupil representatives have distanced themselves, partly over fear of violence [9] [10].

Confidence is high on the planned rallies and Hagel's remarks, reported by tagesschau, Deutschlandfunk, and the Stuttgarter Zeitung via dpa. Confidence is moderate on the Stuttgart organiser's remarks and the intelligence-service line, read only in the headline, standfirst, and caption of a paywalled interview. Hagel's arrest and injury figures were not checked against French official data.

items.title: Germany's Health Minister Won't Rule Out Cuts to Long-Term Care Benefits
items.lede: The number of Germans needing care has risen from two million to more than six million in 20 years, he said, while patient advocates warned families would buckle.

sections.text: Germany's federal health minister Carsten Linnemann (CDU) told the Handelsblatt that long-term care insurance must save around ten per cent and he could not guarantee there would be no benefit cuts [14]. Without reform, the scheme faced a deficit of about eight billion euros in 2027, he said; he rejected compulsory private top-up insurance and criticised the SPD's call to cap residents' own payments in care homes [14]. Eugen Brysch of the German Foundation for Patient Protection said cuts would push the roughly five million people cared for at home, and their relatives, to the brink of collapse [14]. A 13-member government care commission began work this week and is due to make proposals by the end of January [14]. Christos Pantazis, health spokesman for the SPD parliamentary group, told the Rheinische Post that blanket benefit cuts were not inevitable and that efficiency reserves and fairer financing should come first, while VdK president Verena Bentele demanded that cuts be ruled out bindingly [15].
Confidence is high that Linnemann made the remarks, reported by tagesschau from his Handelsblatt interview; no second outlet was read by the cutoff.

items.title: German Prosecutors Say Belarusian Suspects Carried Fuel Canisters to Nuremberg–Würzburg Line
items.lede: Romania also wants both men extradited over a September fire in Brașov, but Bavaria's prosecutors say their own case takes priority.

sections.text: Munich's general prosecutor's office in Germany said on Thursday that two Belarusian men, aged 39 and 50, were caught beside the main Nuremberg–Würzburg rail line at Langenfeld, in Bavaria, with four canisters of highly flammable material [16]. Alexander Ecker, head of Bavaria's extremism and terrorism unit ZET, said they were seen depositing the canisters and were handling them directly at the power and rail line; a power pylon stood nearby, and the exact target is still under investigation [16]. Whether a foreign government or organisation commissioned them is also still under investigation, Ecker said [16]. The men have been in pre-trial custody since 7 October; Der Spiegel first reported the case [17] [18]. Romania, which links them to a 14 September fire at an industrial building next to a state arms firm in Brașov, seeks their extradition, but Ecker said the German case comes first [16] [19]. No Belarusian or Russian statement was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the arrest site, the canisters, and the custody, stated on record by the Munich general prosecutor's office and reported by BR24 and tagesschau. Confidence is moderate on the intended target and any sponsor, which prosecutors say are still under investigation.

items.title: Berlin's New State Parliament Elects Hendrikje Klein as Its First Left Party President
items.lede: Germany's far-right AfD failed to win a vice-presidency in the same secret ballots, leaving one of the two deputy posts vacant for now.

sections.text: The Berlin House of Representatives, the state parliament of Germany's capital, held its constituent session about six weeks after the 20 September election and elected Left Party politician Hendrikje Klein, 46, as president with 98 of 149 votes, 42 against, and nine abstentions [20] [21] [22]. She is the first Left politician in the post and the third woman; the Left, as the largest group, had the right to nominate [20] [22]. AfD candidate Martin Trefzer won only 40 of 149 votes for vice-president, while CDU candidate and former president Cornelia Seibeld was elected with 109; the AfD vote was adjourned, leaving one of the two deputy posts vacant for now [21] [20] [22]. The chamber has 153 seats, 45 of them held by the Left [20].
Confidence is high on the vote figures, stated in the parliament's own notice and reported by tagesschau and rbb24.
